decisions.reason: A same-message MODIFY already fully records the 3.4V DCDC1 source and Schottky OR-ing compensation for this requirement.
A same-message MODIFY already fully records the 3.4V programmed output and its compensation purpose.
Programming DCDC1 to 3.4V before the Schottky diode does not change the monitored rails, monitor device, downstream measurement position, or coverage.
The voltage-compensation decision does not change the number, identity, or separation of project boards.
The source does not necessarily change the existing battery and interboard connector placement or accessibility constraints; the new power-button connector is owned by a separate requirement.
Neither the DCDC1 voltage decision nor the stated power-button connector changes the established board dimensions, orientation, mounting, or enclosure-fit constraints.
The source message already introduces the complete panel-mounted power-control requirement; no additional propagated MODIFY is needed.
The LED requirement continues to use the separate 5V supply and its established level-shifting arrangement; the compensated 3.3V DCDC1 path does not alter it.
The sensor board still receives a regulated 3.3V system rail after the main-board diode, so its connector inventory and signal labels remain valid unchanged.
The source does not change USB data routing, connector sourceability, enumeration, or programming-port behavior.
The new power-board PWRON connector is a distinct panel power-control interface and does not alter the main-board panel-control connector inventory.
The DCDC1 compensation and PWRON button connector do not change the charge-status display or dedicated CHGLED interface.
